passages.text: For example, the leaders among your Egyptians—those who boasted of their study of phenomena aloft and professed to distinguish the natures of the stars—because of an evil suspicion lurking deep within them, subjected it to every dishonor, as far as lay in their power. For some of them handed down the worship of an ox called Apis, others of a male goat, others of a cat, others of a serpent, and even of a fish, onions, winds from bellies, sewers, and limbs of irrational animals, along with countless other utterly shameful absurdities.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Here the phrase introduces the Egyptians as an immediate illustrative case rather than asserting that their conduct occurred at once; a temporal rendering such as “immediately, then” is possible in other contexts.

This takes the adjacent τῶν Αἰγυπτίων ὑμῶν together as “your Egyptians.” Alternatively, ὑμῶν can qualify ἀρχηγέται, yielding “your leaders from among the Egyptians.” The noun ἀρχηγέται can denote leaders, originators, or founders; “leaders” preserves their authoritative role without specifying that they were historical founders.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those who boasted of their study of phenomena aloft
lexical_decisions.rationale: μετεωρολογία denotes inquiry or discourse concerning phenomena aloft, including astronomical and atmospheric matters. “Study of phenomena aloft” preserves both the field-of-study sense and its broader ancient scope, which modern “meteorology” would narrow.

lexical_decisions.chosen: because of an evil suspicion lurking deep within them
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνδομυχέω depicts something dwelling or lurking in the innermost recesses, while ὑπό expresses cause or agency.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πάσῃ αὐτὸ ἀτιμίᾳ ὅσον τὸ κατ’ αὐτοὺς ὑπέβαλαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: subjected it to every dishonor, as far as lay in their power
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter αὐτό has no explicit antecedent within this section, so the translation retains the pronoun rather than identifying its referent in the main text; in the preceding context it most naturally refers to the name under discussion.
τράγος specifically denotes a male goat; the elliptical English continues “handed down the worship” from the preceding clause.
πνεύματα preserves the bodily-wind image, while ὀχετοί denotes drains or sewers in this deliberately degrading list.
